summary: Toast stack with pixel type icons and a draining timer bar that pauses on hover or focus; it can be pinned to a viewport corner.

props.name: position
props.description: Pins the stack to that viewport corner with `position: fixed`, up to 360 px wide. Without it the stack stays in the flow.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum toasts on screen, at least 1; showing one more dismisses the oldest.

props.name: onShow
props.description: Called when a toast is added.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called when a toast starts leaving: timer, dismiss button, action button, overflow or `dismiss()`.

methods.description: Adds a toast and returns its id. `PxToastOptions` is `{ title?: React.ReactNode; description?: React.ReactNode; type?: "info" | "success" | "warning" | "error"; duration?: number; action?: { label: string; onClick?: () => void } }`. `type` defaults to `info` and `duration` to 4500 ms; 0 or less keeps the toast until dismissed. The action button calls `onClick` and dismisses the toast.
Starts the exit of the toast with that id. Unknown or leaving ids are ignored.

accessibility: The stack is a `role="region"` labelled "Notifications". Its list of toasts is the only live region (`aria-live="polite"`): toasts carry no role of their own, so each new toast is announced once, error toasts included.
Dismiss buttons are native buttons labelled "Dismiss"; action buttons use the action label.
A leaving toast is `inert`. If it held focus, focus moves to the dismiss button of the next toast, else of the previous one, else to the region itself (`tabindex="-1"`), never to the page.
Hover or focus inside the stack pauses all timers; they run again once both have left.
The type icons and timer bars are drawn on an `aria-hidden` canvas.
motion: With reduced motion toasts appear and leave without the slide and collapse animations; the timer bars still drain.
notes: Toasts appear only through `show()` on the handle; `ref` is the handle, not the DOM element.
Timers run on timeouts, not in the drawing loop, so toasts also expire while the stack is off screen.
Pinning uses `position: fixed` on the root, so an ancestor that creates a containing block for fixed-position descendants (for example through `filter` or `transform`) changes what it is fixed to.
